metadata.purpose: SmartTransit Delhi Problem 2: join official bus static GTFS with October 2026 ticketing demand summaries

gtfs.publisher: Delhi Transport Corporation / Delhi Integrated Multi-Modal Transit System Ltd.
gtfs.note: GTFS static schedule, not live bus position data. No fare-specific files were present in this archive.

ticketing.name: Delhi October 2026 e-ticketing: historical route/time passenger-demand summaries
ticketing.methodology: Group historical ticket passenger_count by route, weekday/weekend and IST local time slot. For each group, mean passengers per day per hour = sum passenger_count / number of dataset dates of that day type / number of hours in time slot. Within-route demand index = (mean per hour)/(highest mean per hour for SAME route) * 100.
limitations: Historical tickets are not onboard occupancy or live crowding.
Demand indices are normalized separately for each route; do not compare between different routes as occupancy.
A ticketing timestamp does not identify verified bus arrival time.
Route/stop geometry, scheduled trips, service frequencies, validated travel times and true bus capacity require additional data, particularly static bus GTFS.
Dataset records may have errors; invalid rows are excluded.
ticketing.routeMatchMethod: Exact case-insensitive match of ticketing route code to GTFS route_short_name; no fuzzy matching.

limitations: Ticketed passenger counts are historical ticketing demand proxies, not verified onboard occupancy or live crowding.
Ticketing route demand is joined to GTFS only where route codes match exactly; unmatched codes are kept separate.
Within-route demand indices are normalized within each route and must not be compared as absolute occupancy between different routes.
GTFS schedules are static planned times, not real-time arrival predictions.
Segment travel times are derived from scheduled adjacent-stop times across trips; flagged outliers require review.
The archive contains no dedicated fare files, so do not invent fare values.
